name: Stored water
summary: Water already stored somewhere: bottles and jugs, water heaters, pipes, header tanks and toilet cisterns.
uses: Drinking, after treatment if you’re unsure of it
identify: Bottled water and 19-litre cooler jugs in offices and shops; tank water heaters (a 40 or 50 US gallon tank holds about 150 or 190 litres: A.O. Smith gas; cut power or gas and let it cool before draining); water in the pipes of tall buildings, loft header tanks and toilet cisterns (not bowls). Pools and hot tubs hold tonnes of water for washing, cleaning and flushing toilets, never drinking: pool and spa water is for hygiene and cleaning (CDC emergency water, FEMA water fact sheet), and Alberta lists outdoor pools and hot tubs as water to flush toilets with (Alberta water shortage). Pool water can hold high levels of chemicals (Alberta emergency water), and boiling or bleach won't remove chemicals (Ready.gov water).
test: Look and smell: clear and odourless is a good start. Boil or disinfect anything not from a sealed bottle; a filter alone doesn't remove every germ, so disinfect after filtering (CDC make water safe).

decay.note: Sealed bottles keep for years; open tanks grow algae and bacteria.
